Portent

/POR-tent/ - the stress falls on POR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Portent means a sign taken to foretell something, usually something bad.

The harbormaster read the oily green light on the horizon as a portent and ordered every small boat back inside the breakwater.

Worked Example

Biologists took the silence of the frogs as a portent: a marsh that had roared every April had gone quiet, and within three years the tests confirmed what the quiet had promised — the watershed was poisoned.

A portent is a sign with a shadow over it — it points forward, and usually toward trouble. Any clue tells you something about now; a portent makes a claim about what is coming, which is why the word clings to storms, collapses, and bad news still on its way.

How Portent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

omen

omen: the plain word for a sign of things to come, good or bad

warning

warning: a direct alert, spoken or shown, with nothing mystical about it

augury

augury: a formal word for a reading of signs, once done from the flight of birds

Antonyms

reassurance

reassurance: a sign or word that says all is well

memento

memento: a keepsake that points back at the past instead of forward

How Strong Is It? — hint → portent → death knell

hint vs. portent

hint vs. portent: A hint is milder than a portent — a nudge that something may be so, with none of the portent's weight of approaching trouble.

death knell vs. portent

death knell vs. portent: A death knell is stronger than a portent — a portent warns that trouble may be coming, while the knell announces that the end has already arrived.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — por-

Prefix — por-: forward, forth (Latin)

Root — tent

Root — tent: stretched (Latin tendere, 'to stretch')

Put it together

Put it together: Por- (forward) + -tent (stretched, from Latin tendere) = stretched out before you. Latin portendere meant 'to stretch forth, to foreshow': what the gods stretched out in front of an event — the flight of birds, a strange sky — was its portent, the future showing its edge ahead of time.

Use the root in a new word: extend

Use the root in a new word: extend: Workers extend the pier a few meters every summer, stretching it farther into the bay.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Portent belongs to high-stakes forecasting — histories, prophecies, and reports that want a shiver in the sentence. An omen can be lucky; a portent rarely is. For everyday signals, sign or warning does the work without the incense smoke.
